purpose: Machine-readable expert-system KB for general fitness EDUCATION in exercise science and training: it plans, prioritizes, sequences, validates, and risk-controls concrete training work-units (principles, modalities, program design, technique) for finding and applying authoritative training knowledge; it is NOT medical or physiotherapy advice and escalates pain, injury, medical conditions, or special populations to a qualified professional.
assumptions: scope is general fitness education in exercise science and training, not clinical or physiotherapy practice
no observed dataset is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
the trainee is a general adult unless a special population is flagged for escalation
nodes are concrete training work-units, methods, or decision areas
key reference priors: Schoenfeld (hypertrophy) and Rippetoe & Baker (strength programming)
exclusions: clinical management of special populations (pregnancy, cardiac, metabolic, post-surgical)
nutrition prescription beyond general recovery context

competency_questions.question: What is the trainee's primary adaptation goal and baseline, and what constraints and health flags apply?
When must pain, injury, a medical condition, or a special population be escalated to a qualified professional instead of advised?
Which training modalities and energy systems does the goal require and at what emphasis?
How is training stress progressively increased without exceeding recovery?
How is a stall or plateau detected and what triggers a progression change?
How does specificity constrain modality, exercise, and power selection?
How are recovery and accumulated fatigue managed across a training block?
How is the program individualized and autoregulated to the responder?
How are training phases sequenced to manage fatigue and time adaptations?
How are volume, intensity, and frequency set within recoverable limits for the goal?
How are exercises selected, ordered, and coached with sound technique?
What range of motion and warm-up does each selected movement require?
How is non-medical injury risk reduced and when is a clinical issue escalated?
How is progress verified and the program adjusted from objective data?

glossary.definition: systematic increase of training stress over time to drive continued adaptation
the SAID principle: adaptation is specific to the imposed demand
planned variation of training across cycles to manage fatigue and time adaptations
total training work, commonly hard sets per muscle or movement per week
relative load and proximity to failure of the work performed
adjusting load/volume to daily readiness using cues like RPE, RIR, or velocity
a planned reduction in load or volume to dissipate fatigue
training multiple adaptations together, which can cause interference
routing pain, injury, medical conditions, or special populations to a qualified professional
how quickly force is produced, the target of power training
the range of volume a trainee can recover from and adapt to

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established exercise-science and strength-training literature (Schoenfeld 2016, Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy; Rippetoe & Baker, Practical Programming for Strength Training) and coaching practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible
general fitness education only, not medical or physiotherapy advice

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Define the trainee's primary adaptation goal, baseline status, constraints, and health flags before any program is built.
contradictors: lifter who copies a program without a goal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the goal, schedule, equipment, or health status changes

pros.claim: everything downstream is shaped to one goal and one trainee
pros.example: a powerlifting plan and a marathon plan diverge from here

cons.claim: a wrong or vague goal misdirects every later programming choice
cons.example: chasing hypertrophy and a 5k PR in the same block

acceptance_tests: goal is one named adaptation with a measurable target
health/injury flags screened and routed if present
revisit_triggers: new injury or health condition appears

nodes.definition: Detect pain, injury, medical conditions, or special populations and route them to a qualified professional instead of giving training or clinical advice.
contradictors: coach who programs through pain

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when pain, a medical condition, or a special-population status is reported or changes

pros.claim: keeps general fitness education inside its scope and protects the trainee
pros.example: routing sharp joint pain to a clinician instead of coaching through it

cons.claim: over-escalation can stall training for benign soreness
cons.example: treating normal DOMS as a medical event

failure_modes: pain coached as a programming variable
acceptance_tests: any pain/injury/medical/special-population flag triggers referral, not advice
scope-of-practice limit stated explicitly

nodes.definition: Map the goal to the training modalities (strength, hypertrophy, endurance, power, mobility) and their relative emphasis.
contradictors: program that mixes incompatible adaptations equally

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the goal emphasis or trainee priorities shift

pros.claim: prevents interference by ranking competing adaptations
pros.example: strength-first then conditioning for a hybrid goal

cons.claim: over-specializing can leave general capacities weak
cons.example: all max strength, no aerobic base

failure_modes: modality chosen by preference not need
acceptance_tests: each modality emphasis traces to the stated goal

nodes.definition: Specify how training stress is progressively increased over time so adaptation continues without exceeding recovery.
contradictors: lifter who adds load every session regardless of recovery

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when progress stalls or recovery cannot support the current rate

pros.claim: drives continued adaptation without random load jumps
pros.example: adding small weekly increments on a main lift

cons.claim: too-fast progression outruns recovery and raises injury risk
cons.example: adding 10kg a week to a squat

acceptance_tests: progression has an explicit rate and a stall rule

nodes.definition: Ensure the training stimulus matches the target adaptation in movement, velocity, energy system, and context.
contradictors: training that never resembles the target task

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the target task or sport demand changes

pros.claim: training transfers to the actual goal
pros.example: sprint work for a sprinter, not long slow distance

cons.claim: over-specificity reduces general robustness and variety
cons.example: never training outside one movement pattern

acceptance_tests: each selected stimulus maps to a target-task demand

nodes.definition: Manage recovery, sleep, and accumulated fatigue so that training stress produces adaptation rather than overreaching.
contradictors: lifter who treats rest as wasted time

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when fatigue markers rise or sleep/recovery degrade

pros.claim: adaptation is realized only when recovery is adequate
pros.example: a deload restores performance after a hard block

cons.claim: over-caution under-stresses and slows progress
cons.example: resting so much that overload never accrues

acceptance_tests: recovery status has objective markers and a fatigue threshold

nodes.definition: Adjust the program to the individual's response, recovery capacity, preferences, and life context rather than a fixed template.
contradictors: one-size-fits-all template

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the individual's response diverges from the template

pros.claim: matches load to the actual responder and improves adherence
pros.example: using RIR to set daily load instead of fixed percentages

cons.claim: excess individualization can lose programming structure
cons.example: changing the plan every session on feel alone

failure_modes: autoregulation used as an excuse to undertrain
acceptance_tests: at least one autoregulation lever and one adherence accommodation defined

nodes.definition: Sequence training phases (accumulation, intensification, peaking, transition) to manage fatigue and time adaptations.
contradictors: random unstructured training

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the competition date, goal, or fatigue trajectory changes

pros.claim: times peak performance and manages long-term fatigue
pros.example: intensifying before a meet, then deloading

cons.claim: rigid plans break when life disrupts the schedule
cons.example: a fixed 16-week block ignoring missed weeks

failure_modes: phase model chosen by fashion not need
acceptance_tests: phases sequenced with explicit goals and fatigue management

nodes.definition: Set training volume (sets, reps, total work) per muscle/movement to drive adaptation within recoverable limits.

included: minimum effective and maximum recoverable volume

contradictors: junk-volume maximalist

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when recovery cannot support current volume or progress stalls

pros.claim: dosing volume to recoverable limits maximizes adaptation
pros.example: 10-20 hard sets per muscle per week for hypertrophy

cons.claim: too much volume becomes junk and impairs recovery
cons.example: 30 sets that cannot be recovered from

acceptance_tests: weekly volume is within an estimated recoverable range per muscle

nodes.definition: Set relative load and proximity to failure appropriate to the goal modality and phase.
contradictors: lifter who trains to failure every set

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when effort targets no longer match recovery or progress

pros.claim: matches load and effort to the adaptation target
pros.example: heavy low-rep loads for max strength

cons.claim: constant failure training erodes recovery and form
cons.example: grinding every set to failure

failure_modes: failure used as the only intensity tool
acceptance_tests: intensity expressed in an explicit unit and matched to the goal

nodes.definition: Decide how often each muscle/movement is trained per week and how sessions are organized.
contradictors: one weekly session per muscle by default

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when schedule or recovery changes the feasible frequency

pros.claim: distributing volume across sessions improves quality and recovery
pros.example: hitting a muscle twice weekly instead of once

cons.claim: too-high frequency without recovery causes interference
cons.example: daily heavy work on the same lift

acceptance_tests: frequency distributes the prescribed weekly volume feasibly

nodes.definition: Choose and order exercises that match the target adaptation, fit available equipment, and respect joint health.
contradictors: program built only from favorite exercises

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when equipment, joint health, or movement priorities change

pros.claim: exercises chosen for transfer and joint health beat random picks
pros.example: choosing a hinge variant that fits the lifter's mobility

cons.claim: novelty-seeking selection breaks progression tracking
cons.example: swapping exercises every week

acceptance_tests: each exercise maps to a movement pattern and respects joint-health flags

nodes.definition: Establish sound movement technique using basic biomechanics so load is applied safely and effectively.

included: form standards and ranges of motion

contradictors: lifter who chases load over form

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a technical fault or pain appears under load

pros.claim: sound technique lets load progress with lower injury risk
pros.example: bracing and a neutral spine on a deadlift

cons.claim: over-coaching form can stall practical progress
cons.example: endless mobility drills with no loaded practice

failure_modes: cues address symptoms not the fault
acceptance_tests: technique standard and at least one fault-correction cue per main lift
pain under load routes to escalation

nodes.definition: Build the range of motion and warm-up needed to train the selected movements well and safely.
contradictors: lifter who skips warm-up entirely

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a movement's range-of-motion demand is unmet

pros.claim: adequate range and warm-up enable full-range, lower-risk training
pros.example: hip mobility that allows a full-depth squat

cons.claim: excess mobility work displaces actual training time
cons.example: 45 minutes of stretching before lifting

acceptance_tests: each main movement has the range and warm-up it requires

nodes.definition: Develop maximal force production through heavy compound training and neural/structural adaptation.
contradictors: high-rep-only trainee expecting max strength

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when strength progress stalls or test results plateau

pros.claim: heavy compound loading builds transferable maximal force
pros.example: low-rep squats and deadlifts driving a 1RM up

cons.claim: heavy loading raises technical and joint-stress risk
cons.example: maxing out with degraded form

acceptance_tests: strength work uses loads and rep ranges that drive maximal force

nodes.definition: Drive muscle growth through sufficient volume, effort, and mechanical tension across a controlled range.
contradictors: lifter expecting growth from minimal volume

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when growth stalls at current volume and effort

pros.claim: sufficient volume at high effort across full ROM grows muscle
pros.example: 10-20 hard sets per muscle through a full range

cons.claim: chasing volume past recovery yields junk sets
cons.example: adding sets that cannot be recovered

failure_modes: volume or effort below the growth threshold
acceptance_tests: hypertrophy work meets a volume and effort threshold over a controlled ROM

nodes.definition: Develop aerobic and muscular endurance by targeting the relevant energy systems at appropriate intensities and durations.
contradictors: only-sprints trainee expecting an aerobic base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when endurance markers plateau or interfere with strength goals

pros.claim: targeting the right energy system builds the needed endurance
pros.example: building an aerobic base before adding intervals

cons.claim: high endurance volume can blunt strength/hypertrophy gains
cons.example: long runs the day before heavy squats

failure_modes: intensity distribution wrong for the goal
acceptance_tests: endurance work targets the energy system the goal requires

nodes.definition: Train rate of force development through ballistic, plyometric, and velocity-based work built on a strength base.
contradictors: novice doing depth jumps without a strength base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when landing mechanics degrade or the strength base is insufficient

pros.claim: plyometric and velocity work raise rate of force development
pros.example: box jumps and med-ball throws after a strength base

cons.claim: high-impact plyometrics on a weak base raise injury risk
cons.example: depth jumps before basic strength exists

failure_modes: plyometrics prescribed without a strength prerequisite
acceptance_tests: plyometric progression gates on a strength prerequisite and sound landing mechanics
pain or poor landings route to escalation

nodes.definition: Schedule planned reductions in load/volume to dissipate fatigue and realize adaptation or peak performance.
contradictors: lifter who never deloads

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when accumulated fatigue exceeds the planned threshold

pros.claim: planned deloads convert accumulated work into adaptation
pros.example: a lighter week restoring bar speed and motivation

cons.claim: unneeded deloads interrupt momentum
cons.example: deloading on a fixed clock despite low fatigue

failure_modes: taper mistimed before a goal event
acceptance_tests: deload/taper has an explicit trigger and structure

nodes.definition: Track performance, load, and readiness metrics to verify the program is working and to drive adjustments.
contradictors: lifter who never logs anything

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when logged data shows a stall, regression, or readiness drop

pros.claim: objective tracking turns guesses into evidence-based adjustments
pros.example: logging bar speed to detect an early stall

cons.claim: over-measuring can distract from training itself
cons.example: chasing every metric instead of training

failure_modes: data collected but never acted on
acceptance_tests: at least one objective progress metric and an adjustment rule exist
revisit_triggers: a stall or regression is logged

nodes.definition: Reduce non-medical injury risk through load management, recovery, and technique guardrails, escalating anything clinical.
contradictors: coach who ignores warning signs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when load spikes, warning signs appear, or any pain/medical flag is reported

pros.claim: managing load and technique lowers preventable injury risk
pros.example: capping weekly load jumps and fixing form faults early

cons.claim: conservative caps can under-stimulate adaptation
cons.example: never letting load progress for fear of injury

failure_modes: pain treated as a training variable instead of escalated
acceptance_tests: a load-management rule and an escalation trigger are both defined
any pain/medical flag routes to a qualified professional
revisit_triggers: any pain or medical condition reported

edges.why_related: screening for escalation requires the trainee's goal, history, and flags
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scope safety is set before programming
edges.risk_of_conflict: programming over an unscreened medical issue
edges.example: sharp knee pain found during intake
edges.resolution_rule: screen before any program advice

edges.why_related: modality selection is driven by the stated goal and profile
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong modality mix for the goal
edges.example: picking endurance work for a strength goal
edges.resolution_rule: fix goal before selecting modalities

edges.why_related: the overload scheme is built for the chosen modalities
edges.example: adding reps when strength needs load
edges.resolution_rule: select modalities before the overload scheme

edges.why_related: specificity constraints follow from the chosen modalities
edges.example: general work for a specific sport
edges.resolution_rule: set modalities before specificity

edges.why_related: recovery is managed against the overload being applied
edges.example: weekly load jumps with no rest week
edges.resolution_rule: define overload before managing its recovery

edges.why_related: phases sequence and modulate the overload over time
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fatigue is managed across the plan
edges.example: linear adds with no phase logic
edges.resolution_rule: establish overload before periodizing it

edges.why_related: individual adjustment rules need the baseline profile
edges.risk_of_conflict: template applied to the wrong person
edges.example: fixed percentages for an unknown responder
edges.resolution_rule: profile the trainee before individualizing

edges.why_related: volume is dosed within recoverable limits
edges.example: 30 unrecoverable sets
edges.resolution_rule: know recovery capacity before dosing volume

edges.why_related: volume targets are set per phase
edges.example: same volume in a deload week
edges.resolution_rule: periodize before fixing volume

edges.why_related: intensity targets are set per phase
edges.example: heavy singles in an accumulation block
edges.resolution_rule: periodize before fixing intensity

edges.why_related: autoregulated intensity needs individual rules
edges.example: percentages on a bad-sleep day
edges.resolution_rule: set individualization before autoregulated intensity

edges.why_related: frequency distributes the prescribed weekly volume
edges.benefit_of_coupling: volume is split into recoverable sessions
edges.risk_of_conflict: frequency that cannot fit the volume
edges.example: all volume in one session
edges.resolution_rule: fix volume before distributing it

edges.why_related: exercise choices must satisfy specificity constraints
edges.example: novelty exercises with no transfer
edges.resolution_rule: apply specificity before selecting exercises

edges.why_related: selection and order depend on the session split
edges.example: too many big lifts in one session
edges.resolution_rule: fix the split before selecting exercises

edges.why_related: technique standards are set for the selected exercises
edges.risk_of_conflict: loading exercises with no form standard
edges.example: heavy pulls with no bracing standard
edges.resolution_rule: select exercises before setting technique standards

edges.why_related: warm-up and mobility are built for the technique demands
edges.benefit_of_coupling: movements have the range they need
edges.risk_of_conflict: training movements out of available range
edges.example: squatting deep without hip range
edges.resolution_rule: set technique before mobility prep

edges.why_related: strength blocks need heavy intensity targets
edges.example: high reps expecting max strength
edges.resolution_rule: set intensity before the strength block

edges.why_related: heavy strength work requires sound technique first
edges.example: grinding reps with a rounded back
edges.resolution_rule: secure technique before heavy strength work

edges.why_related: hypertrophy needs sufficient prescribed volume
edges.example: too few hard sets
edges.resolution_rule: set volume before the hypertrophy block

edges.why_related: hypertrophy needs adequate effort/intensity
edges.example: stopping far from failure
edges.resolution_rule: set effort targets before the hypertrophy block

edges.why_related: endurance work targets the prioritized energy systems
edges.example: all sprints for an aerobic goal
edges.resolution_rule: prioritize energy systems before endurance work

edges.why_related: power and plyometrics require a strength base
edges.benefit_of_coupling: force can be expressed fast safely
edges.example: depth jumps before basic strength
edges.resolution_rule: build a strength base before power/plyometrics

edges.why_related: power work is matched to the specific velocity demand
edges.example: random plyos unrelated to the sport
edges.resolution_rule: apply specificity to power work

edges.why_related: deloads are triggered by fatigue status
edges.example: training through deep fatigue
edges.resolution_rule: read fatigue before scheduling a deload

edges.why_related: tapers are placed within the phase plan
edges.example: tapering two weeks too early
edges.resolution_rule: place deload/taper within the periodized plan

edges.why_related: tracking verifies the overload is working
edges.example: no stall signal until regression
edges.resolution_rule: define overload before tracking it

edges.why_related: load management builds on recovery and fatigue status
edges.example: huge weekly load jumps
edges.resolution_rule: manage recovery before load-management rules

edges.why_related: technique guardrails are part of risk reduction
edges.example: adding weight to a failing pattern
edges.resolution_rule: fix technique before relying on load caps

edges.why_related: escalation scope bounds what load management may do without a clinician
edges.example: programming around undiagnosed pain
edges.resolution_rule: any medical flag overrides load tweaks and escalates

edges.why_related: pain under load must escalate rather than be cued away
edges.example: cueing through joint pain
edges.resolution_rule: pain under load escalates, not coaches

edges.why_related: individual recovery capacity bounds prescribable volume
edges.example: 20-set template for a low-recovery trainee
edges.resolution_rule: individual recovery capacity caps template volume

edges.why_related: fatigue signals trigger revisiting the overload rate
edges.example: pushing load while fatigue climbs
edges.resolution_rule: if fatigue exceeds threshold, reduce overload rate; stop when markers normalize

edges.why_related: tracked stalls trigger adjusting the progression
edges.example: logging a stall but not changing load
edges.resolution_rule: on a logged stall, adjust progression; stop when progress resumes

edges.why_related: higher volume and higher intensity compete for limited recovery
edges.example: max sets at max effort every session
edges.resolution_rule: periodize emphasis: prioritize one per phase; recovery dominates

edges.why_related: concurrent strength and endurance create interference
edges.example: heavy lifting and long runs daily
edges.resolution_rule: sequence or separate sessions; the primary goal dominates emphasis

edges.why_related: growth-driving volume competes with recovery capacity
edges.example: adding sets until sleep suffers
edges.resolution_rule: cap volume at recoverable limits; recovery dominates

edges.why_related: pushing load competes with maintaining sound technique
edges.example: adding weight as form breaks down
edges.resolution_rule: technique quality dominates; load waits for the standard

edges.why_related: warm-up/mobility should precede heavy strength work
edges.example: first set is a heavy single
edges.resolution_rule: warm up and prep before heavy work

edges.why_related: both use resistance training but target different adaptations
edges.example: using a strength block expecting growth
edges.resolution_rule: keep dosing distinct; share only the movement library

edges.why_related: monitored fatigue and stalls change deload timing
edges.example: missing a needed deload
edges.resolution_rule: let monitoring data set deload timing

conflict_axes.trigger: high volume and high intensity both compete for limited recovery
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: recovery capacity dominates; one variable is emphasized per phase
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if both are maximized and fatigue markers spike
conflict_axes.example: max sets at max effort every session

conflict_axes.trigger: training strength and endurance together blunts one adaptation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the stated primary goal dominates emphasis; interference is minimized by separation
conflict_axes.example: long runs the day before heavy squats

conflict_axes.trigger: pushing load competes with maintaining sound technique
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: technique quality dominates; load waits for the standard
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if form breaks down or pain appears under load
conflict_axes.example: adding weight as the rep rounds the back

conflict_axes.trigger: growth-driving volume competes with recoverable capacity
resolution_order: add volume only if recovery holds
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: recovery dominates; volume above recoverable capacity is junk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if added sets degrade sleep or performance

conflict_axes.trigger: specific training competes with variety and general robustness
resolution_order: anchor primary lifts to the goal
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: specificity dominates primary work; variety is allowed in accessories
conflict_axes.example: swapping the main lift every week

conflict_axes.trigger: faster progression competes with managing injury risk
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: risk management dominates; progression stays within load caps
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a load spike or warning sign appears

conflict_axes.trigger: a fixed periodized plan competes with autoregulating to daily readiness
resolution_order: revisit the plan if response diverges
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: phase intent sets the frame; autoregulation tunes within it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if readiness chronically conflicts with the plan
conflict_axes.example: forcing planned percentages on a poor-recovery day

conflict_axes.trigger: a desire to keep training competes with the need to escalate a clinical issue
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: medical-boundary escalation dominates; general fitness education never substitutes for clinical care
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: any pain, injury, medical condition, or special population (pregnancy, cardiac, etc.)
conflict_axes.example: coaching through sharp joint pain instead of referring

edge_cases.trigger: pain is treated as a training variable to coach around
edge_cases.failure_mode: clinical issue programmed instead of escalated
edge_cases.example: adding load to a painful joint
edge_cases.detection_method: any pain/injury/medical flag in inputs must map to escalation

edge_cases.example: weekly PR attempts with no rest week
edge_cases.detection_method: check progression rate against recovery markers and deload schedule
check weekly volume against an estimated recoverable range
resolution: trim volume to the recoverable range

edge_cases.trigger: plyometrics prescribed without a strength base
edge_cases.failure_mode: high-impact work on an unprepared athlete
edge_cases.detection_method: gate plyometrics on a strength prerequisite check

edge_cases.trigger: concurrent strength and endurance maximized together
edge_cases.example: daily heavy lifting and long runs
edge_cases.detection_method: check session ordering and primary-goal emphasis

edge_cases.failure_mode: reinforced faulty pattern and injury risk
edge_cases.example: grinding reps with a rounding spine
edge_cases.detection_method: check that load increments require meeting the technique standard
resolution: hold load until the standard is met

edge_cases.example: never deloading across a long block
edge_cases.detection_method: check deload trigger against fatigue markers

edge_cases.trigger: program built without a single clear goal
edge_cases.example: chasing a 5k PR and a squat PR in one block
edge_cases.detection_method: check each modality emphasis traces to one stated goal

edge_cases.trigger: a special population is given generic programming
edge_cases.failure_mode: unsafe load for pregnancy, cardiac, or post-surgical status
edge_cases.example: a generic high-intensity plan during pregnancy
edge_cases.detection_method: check special-population status flags before prescribing

edge_cases.trigger: no objective progress metric is tracked
edge_cases.example: training for months with no logs
edge_cases.detection_method: check at least one objective metric and an adjustment rule exist

workflow.objective: fix the goal and screen for escalation before any programming
acceptance_tests: goal is one named adaptation
every health flag is screened and routed
workflow.do_first_because: nothing downstream is valid or safe until the goal and health flags are settled

workflow.objective: map the goal to modalities, energy systems, and specificity constraints
acceptance_tests: each modality emphasis traces to the goal
exit_criteria: modality plan and specificity constraints set
workflow.do_first_because: modality and specificity choices drive every later programming variable

workflow.objective: set the overload, recovery, and individualization rules
acceptance_tests: progression has a rate and a stall rule
recovery has objective markers
workflow.do_first_because: overload and recovery rules govern how all phases and doses behave

acceptance_tests: phases sequenced with explicit goals
deload has a trigger and structure
exit_criteria: phase plan and deload schedule set
workflow.do_first_because: phase structure frames the volume, intensity, and frequency doses

workflow.objective: set volume, intensity, and frequency within recoverable limits
acceptance_tests: weekly volume is within a recoverable range
intensity and frequency match the goal
workflow.do_first_because: the dose determines whether the phase produces adaptation or junk fatigue

workflow.objective: select and order exercises and set technique and warm-up standards
acceptance_tests: each exercise maps to a pattern and respects joint-health flags
each main lift has a technique standard

workflow.objective: build the modality-specific blocks on the prepared base
acceptance_tests: each modality block meets its dosing threshold

priority_rationale.notes: tunes the plan to the responder
power block gated on a base

dominance_rules.trigger: any pain, injury, medical condition, or special population is present
dominance_rules.rule: escalation to a qualified professional dominates over giving training advice
dominance_rules.required_action: route to a clinician and withhold prescription within scope
dominance_rules.example: referring sharp joint pain instead of programming around it

dominance_rules.trigger: added volume or load outruns recovery
dominance_rules.rule: recovery capacity dominates over more volume or intensity
dominance_rules.required_action: cap the dose at recoverable limits

dominance_rules.rule: technique quality dominates over adding load
dominance_rules.required_action: hold load until the standard is met
dominance_rules.example: keeping the bar light until bracing is solid

dominance_rules.rule: risk management dominates over rapid progression
the stated primary goal dominates emphasis
dominance_rules.required_action: separate or sequence the interfering work
dominance_rules.example: strength-first, conditioning trimmed for a strength goal

dominance_rules.trigger: a valuable node lacks its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates over value-first ordering

dominance_rules.trigger: a node has risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or an irreversible decision
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates over automated finalization
dominance_rules.required_action: require sign-off before locking high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.example: a coach approves before a max test

dominance_rules.rule: QA dominates over locking the program
dominance_rules.required_action: do not hard-lock until checks pass
dominance_rules.example: holding the block open until the dry run passes

dominance_rules.trigger: a number looks precise but is only heuristic
dominance_rules.rule: correct evidence labeling dominates over false precision
dominance_rules.example: marking estimated set targets as heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: an object lacks source or reference support
dominance_rules.rule: traceability dominates over adding unsupported objects

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the goal and profile before designing the program
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a program built for the wrong goal is reworked wholesale
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: modality plan changes after the goal is clarified
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a split before knowing the goal

anti_rework_rules.rule: screen for medical/special-population flags before prescribing load
anti_rework_rules.rationale: prescribing over an unscreened issue causes harm and full redo
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a flag surfaces after the program is built

anti_rework_rules.rule: select modalities before the overload scheme
anti_rework_rules.rationale: progressing the wrong variable wastes a block
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: progression variable changes after modality choice
anti_rework_rules.example: adding reps when strength needs load

anti_rework_rules.rule: periodize before fixing volume and intensity
anti_rework_rules.rationale: doses set without phases get re-cut every week
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: doses change once phases are added

anti_rework_rules.rule: know recovery capacity before dosing volume
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: volume is cut after recovery fails

anti_rework_rules.rule: select exercises before setting technique standards
anti_rework_rules.rationale: technique work on dropped exercises is wasted
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: standards are written for exercises later cut
anti_rework_rules.example: coaching a lift that gets removed

anti_rework_rules.rule: secure technique before heavy or plyometric work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: heavy or impact work on bad form causes injury and redo
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: load is pulled back after a form breakdown

anti_rework_rules.rule: build a strength base before power/plyometrics
anti_rework_rules.rationale: plyometrics on a weak base risk injury and a restart
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: plyometrics are removed after a failed landing

anti_rework_rules.rule: run validation and risk review before hard-locking
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before review forces costly unlocking
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a defect is found after the lock

anti_rework_rules.rule: require human review before irreversible high-risk decisions
anti_rework_rules.rationale: irreversible decisions made by automation cause harm
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an irreversible choice was made without sign-off
anti_rework_rules.example: a max test approved without a coach

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or a dry run reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream impact
action: score defects by risk and coupling
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect is first

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and edges of the affected node
acceptance_tests: all dependents identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is routed for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: apply the repair via the responsible subsystem
acceptance_tests: the specific check now passes

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the formula script over all derived fields
action: recompute final_importance, risk_score, posterior, edge scores
acceptance_tests: all formulas pass within 0.02

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator in dense mode
acceptance_tests: overall_status is pass
posterior matches the no-observed-data formula

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect requires human judgment or a medical/special-population flag is involved
acceptance_tests: a decision record exists

iteration_protocol.detection: compare counts and check results against the prior version
acceptance_tests: no new failures vs prior

human_review_required_for: any pain, injury, medical condition, or special population
hard lock of the finalized program

checks.repair_action: modeled volume/intensity, concurrent, and load/technique tensions as conflict edges, not dependencies
recomputed all derived fields via formula script

test_cases.input_summary: a trainee reports sharp joint pain
a pregnant trainee asks for a generic plan
max volume and max intensity in one phase
heavy lifting and long runs daily

expected_properties: POWER_AND_PLYOMETRICS gates on a strength base

change_triggers: a medical or special-population flag appears
an injury or pain is reported
monitoring data shows a stall or regression
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked program change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade on a failed dry run or readiness drop
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: any pain, injury, medical condition, or special population
hard lock of the finalized program
